Shewbread
SHOW-bred
n.
Shew (archaic for show) + bread; renders the Hebrew lechem ha-pānīm, literally bread of the face or bread of the presence; the twelve loaves placed weekly on the gold table in the holy place of the tabernacle and temple.

Biblical Definition

The shewbread (literally bread of the face/presence) was the twelve loaves placed weekly on the gold table in the holy place of the tabernacle, and subsequently of the temple, throughout the Old Testament period. Leviticus 24:5-9 prescribes the ritual: and thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deals shall be in one cake. And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the LORD. And thou shalt put pure frankincense upon each row, that it may be on the bread for a memorial, even an offering made by fire unto the LORD. Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; and they shall eat it in the holy place: for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the LORD made by fire by a perpetual statute. Several structural features mark the doctrine. First, the twelve loaves represented the twelve tribes of Israel—the whole covenant people set before the LORD perpetually as the bread of His presence. Second, the loaves were placed in the holy place, the second of the tabernacle’s three zones (the court, the holy place, the holy of holies); they stood opposite the gold lampstand, with the altar of incense between the table and the veil. Third, the loaves were replaced weekly on the Sabbath; the old loaves were eaten by the priests in the holy place—a perpetual covenantal communion-meal between the priests representing the people and the LORD before whom the bread was set. Fourth, the bread was continually before the LORD—there was never a moment in tabernacle or temple history when the bread of the presence was absent from the gold table. The shewbread therefore has several theological functions. Liturgically: a perpetual memorial of the covenant relationship between the LORD and His people, with the people’s representative-bread always before His face. Typologically: pointing toward the Christ who would Himself be the bread of life, given to the church as the perpetual sustenance of the people of God. Ecclesially: anticipating the Lord’s Supper at which the bread of the Lord’s body is given to the saints as the covenantal meal of the new covenant. Christ’s reference to the shewbread in Matthew 12:3-4 (defending His disciples’ eating of corn on the Sabbath by appealing to David’s eating of the shewbread in 1 Sam 21) shows His use of the shewbread-history for pastoral and theological argument: the ceremonial law’s details serve God’s purpose for His people; the Sabbath itself is for man and not man for the Sabbath; the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath. The shewbread-typology continues into the New Covenant: the bread of His presence becomes the bread of the Lord’s table, given to His new covenant people as the perpetual memorial of His body broken for them and the sign of their covenantal communion with Him.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines SHEWBREAD as the bread of the presence; twelve loaves placed every sabbath on the holy table in the tabernacle and temple, representing the twelve tribes of Israel and serving as a perpetual covenantal memorial.

SHEWBREAD, n. — Among the Jews, bread of exhibition; the twelve loaves of bread which the priest of the week placed before the Lord on the golden table in the sanctuary. They were renewed every Sabbath, and only the priests were permitted to eat them.

SHEW, v.t. — (Archaic for SHOW.) To exhibit or present to the view of another; to set before.

Key Scripture

Leviticus 24:5-8 — "And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deals shall be in one cake. And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the LORD. And thou shalt put pure frankincense upon each row, that it may be on the bread for a memorial, even an offering made by fire unto the LORD. Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually..."

Exodus 25:30 — "And thou shalt set upon the table shewbread before me alway."

Matthew 12:3-4 — "But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him; How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?"

John 6:35 — "And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst."

Modern Corruption

The shewbread-doctrine is corrupted in much contemporary preaching by the general loss of typological reading that no longer traces the tabernacle furnishings to their Christological and ecclesial fulfillments—and by the inverse over-allegorization in some traditions that extracts arbitrary spiritual meaning from every architectural detail without grounding in the typological-Christological substance the New Testament itself authorizes.

expand to see more

The general loss of typological reading in much contemporary preaching is the broader corruption that affects the shewbread along with other tabernacle furnishings. The twelve loaves of presence-bread are taught (where they are taught at all) as ancient cultic detail without serious tracing to their Christological substance: Christ as the bread of life, the church as the new covenant people whose representative-bread is now the bread of the Lord’s table, the Sabbath-renewal of the shewbread anticipating the Sabbath-rest of the new covenant. The recovery is the recovery of typological reading itself, with the New Testament’s own treatment as the controlling guide. Christ’s appeal to the shewbread in defense of His Sabbath ministry (Matt 12:3-4) authorizes typological-pastoral use of the detail; John 6’s great I am the bread of life discourse provides the Christological substance the shewbread-typology was always pointing toward; the Lord’s table provides the new covenant’s perpetual covenantal meal that the shewbread was forever anticipating.

The opposite corruption is the over-allegorization in some traditions that extracts arbitrary spiritual meaning from every architectural detail (the precise dimensions of the table, the specific number of horns on the altar, the colors of the curtains) without grounding in the typological-Christological substance the New Testament itself authorizes. Tabernacle-allegorizing of this kind has, in some preaching traditions, produced sermons of impressive ingenuity and dubious doctrinal weight; the imagined meanings often have no biblical basis and shift from preacher to preacher. The biblical balance is precise. Typological reading is authorized where the NT itself does it (Christ as bread of life for the shewbread; Christ as light of the world for the lampstand; Christ as Mediator for the veil); typological inference is appropriate where it is grounded in the NT’s own pattern; bare allegorization of details the NT does not address is to be avoided. The shewbread-typology, well-anchored in John 6 and the Lord’s table, stands; the over-allegorizations of impressive-but-ungrounded inventiveness do not. The recovery of disciplined typological reading is the path between the loss of typology and its over-extension.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew lechem ha-pānīm (bread of the face/presence); the twelve loaves placed weekly on the gold table of the tabernacle and temple, representing the twelve tribes of Israel and pointing typologically to the Christ who is the bread of life and to the bread of the Lord’s table in the new covenant.

expand to see more

Hebrew lechem ha-pānīm (H3899 + H6440) — bread of the presence (literally bread of the face).

Hebrew ma‘areketh (H4635) — the row, arrangement (the technical term for the shewbread arrangement).

Greek artoi tēs protheseōs — bread of the presentation (LXX/NT term; Matt 12:4; Mark 2:26; Luke 6:4; Heb 9:2).

Greek artos (G740) — bread (John 6:35, the bread of life; the Lord’s Supper’s bread).

Usage

"The twelve loaves of shewbread represented the twelve tribes of Israel, the whole covenant people set before the LORD perpetually as the bread of His presence."

"Christ’s appeal to the shewbread in defense of His Sabbath ministry (Matt 12:3-4) authorizes the typological reading of OT cultic detail for NT pastoral substance."

"The shewbread is fulfilled in Christ the Bread of Life (John 6:35) and in the bread of the Lord’s table given to the new covenant people of God."
